question: A 21-year-old lacrosse player comes to the doctor for an annual health assessment. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. She is 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weighs 57 kg (125 lb); BMI is 22 kg/m2. Pulmonary function tests show an FEV1 of 90% and an FVC of 3600 mL. Whole body plethysmography is performed to measure airway resistance. Which of the following structures of the respiratory tree is likely to have the highest contribution to total airway resistance?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Airway resistance is influenced by the diameter of the airways" -> "Smaller airways have higher resistance" -> "Terminal bronchioles are smaller than segmental bronchi" -> "Terminal bronchioles contribute significantly to total airway resistance" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Airway resistance is highest in the smaller airways" -> "Conducting bronchioles are larger than terminal bronchioles" -> "Terminal bronchioles are the last part of the conducting zone" -> "Terminal bronchioles likely have the highest contribution to total airway resistance" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Total airway resistance is determined by the sum of resistances in all airways" -> "Mainstem bronchi are larger and have lower resistance" -> "Segmental bronchi are also larger than terminal bronchioles" -> "Terminal bronchioles are the smallest conducting airways" -> "Terminal bronchioles likely have the highest contribution to total airway resistance" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Airway resistance increases as airway diameter decreases" -> "Respiratory bronchioles are part of the respiratory zone" -> "Conducting bronchioles precede respiratory bronchioles" -> "Terminal bronchioles are the last segment of the conducting zone" -> "Terminal bronchioles likely have the highest contribution to total airway resistance" -> 75%
analysis: Airway resistance in the respiratory tree is primarily determined by the diameter of the airways. The conducting airways, particularly the bronchi and bronchioles, contribute significantly to total airway resistance. Among the options provided, the terminal bronchioles (option opd) are the smallest conducting airways and have a significant contribution to resistance due to their smaller diameter. However, the segmental bronchi (option opc) are larger and have a greater overall cross-sectional area compared to the terminal bronchioles, making them a major contributor to airway resistance. Therefore, the segmental bronchi are likely to have the highest contribution to total airway resistance.
